sections.title: CORE ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
sections.finding: Reviewed publish snapshots exist; confirmations are inconsistent for disconnect, administration and legacy routes.
sections.next_action: Define one action-risk policy and enforce its confirmation and audit rules across every mutation.

sections.title: MULTI-TENANCY
sections.finding: Canonical workspace/owner membership backfill and atomic account/brand provisioning are implemented. Current owner-scoped routes enforce live capability checks; permission changes revoke sessions and queued Studio/older scheduled jobs recheck publishing authority. Shared-team routing, canonical workspace references on every object, legacy authority consolidation and database RLS remain incomplete. A versioned offline migration now backfills canonical references on all 16 brand-owned tables and installs database write guards for owner/brand/reference immutability. Isolated tests cover direct SQL attacks and existing ORM compatibility; runtime read isolation, RLS, account-level/legacy mapping and deployment remain incomplete. Offline migration lock/statement waits are now bounded and reference previews reject existing incorrect mappings; PostgreSQL contention, cancellation, rollback and retry tests passed at 09c5771; runtime read isolation and deployment remain open. Canonical references now map into all brand-owned ORM records and scoped content reads. Fresh schema setup installs guards; existing populated databases require offline reference migration before startup. Runtime SQLite/PostgreSQL regression and synthetic restore passed at dc55d2b; PostgreSQL RLS and complete service authority remain open.
sections.next_action: Add immutable workspace references and lifecycle constraints, complete shared-member route/worker authorization, and enforce restricted-role PostgreSQL RLS before rollout.

sections.title: AUTHENTICATION
sections.finding: Optional TOTP enrollment, encrypted secrets, one-use recovery codes, expiring version-bound challenges, replay/rate controls and password/Apple enforcement are implemented in the integration candidate. Existing users are not enrolled. New passwords retain the 15-character policy. Maintained compromised-password screening, privileged mandatory MFA and operational recovery assurance remain incomplete.
sections.next_action: Validate PostgreSQL/restore and browser journeys, obtain security review, establish verified recovery operations and privileged MFA rollout; add maintained compromised-password screening.

sections.title: AUTHORIZATION
sections.finding: Canonical workspace/owner membership backfill and atomic account/brand provisioning are implemented. Current owner-scoped routes enforce live capability checks; permission changes revoke sessions and queued Studio/older scheduled jobs recheck publishing authority. Shared-team routing, canonical workspace references on every object, legacy authority consolidation and database RLS remain incomplete. Canonical references now map into all brand-owned ORM records and scoped content reads. Fresh schema setup installs guards; existing populated databases require offline reference migration before startup. Runtime SQLite/PostgreSQL regression and synthetic restore passed at dc55d2b; PostgreSQL RLS and complete service authority remain open.
sections.next_action: Add immutable workspace references and lifecycle constraints, complete shared-member route/worker authorization, and enforce restricted-role PostgreSQL RLS before rollout.

sections.title: SOCIAL PLATFORM CONNECTION SECURITY
sections.finding: Provider OAuth state and encrypted tokens exist. Disconnect clears local tokens but lacks a complete remote-revocation, audit and scheduled-work cancellation workflow.
sections.next_action: Implement provider-specific revocation and transactional local cancellation; test expired state, wrong scope, disconnect races and secret masking.

sections.title: PUBLISHING ARCHITECTURE
sections.finding: Reviewed Studio and legacy Custom GPT publishing now persist durable jobs before responding. Legacy submissions have creator-scoped idempotency, immutable approval fields, status and conditional cancellation; worker claims and ambiguous outcomes are tested. New action-contract rollout and operational proof remain outstanding.
sections.next_action: Validate the new legacy action contract and additive migration in isolated staging when the deferral ends; finish canonical tenant mapping, provider-specific recovery and operational assurance.

sections.title: CONCURRENCY
sections.finding: Draft revisions, conditional job claims and selected transactions exist. Concurrency guarantees do not cover all mutable resources and disconnect races.
sections.next_action: Extend versioned writes and concurrency tests to account, schedule, strategy, connection and billing boundaries.

sections.title: QUEUES AND WORKERS
sections.finding: Studio and legacy X publish work is durable and conditionally claimed. A dedicated worker entry point is implemented; web embedding can be disabled. Classified retry/backpressure and complete dead-letter operations for all external work remain incomplete.
sections.next_action: Introduce recoverable claim/lease, retry classification and inspect/retry/cancel tooling without replaying ambiguous external actions.

sections.title: RATE LIMITING
sections.finding: Database mutation/auth/AI limits exist; reads and provider-specific quota controllers are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Add endpoint/resource budgets and per-provider quota backpressure with concurrent boundary tests.

sections.title: DATABASE DESIGN
sections.finding: SQLAlchemy relational entities and PostgreSQL support exist, but workspace identity and important state remain spread across legacy and JSON fields. A versioned offline migration now backfills canonical references on all 16 brand-owned tables and installs database write guards for owner/brand/reference immutability. Isolated tests cover direct SQL attacks and existing ORM compatibility; runtime read isolation, RLS, account-level/legacy mapping and deployment remain incomplete. Offline migration lock/statement waits are now bounded and reference previews reject existing incorrect mappings; PostgreSQL contention, cancellation, rollback and retry tests passed at 09c5771; runtime read isolation and deployment remain open. Canonical references now map into all brand-owned ORM records and scoped content reads. Fresh schema setup installs guards; existing populated databases require offline reference migration before startup. Runtime SQLite/PostgreSQL regression and synthetic restore passed at dc55d2b; PostgreSQL RLS and complete service authority remain open.
sections.next_action: Review canonical relational constraints and migrate ownership with reconciliation and rollback evidence.

sections.title: DATABASE SECURITY
sections.finding: Production private networking, TLS enforcement and restricted identities cannot be proved from this checkout; migrations run during application import.
sections.next_action: Supply deployment configuration evidence and separate migration/application/worker identities with least privilege.

sections.title: DATABASE BACKUPS
sections.finding: CI exercises a synthetic PostgreSQL restore. Current production RPO/RTO, encryption and a measured production-like recovery drill are not evidenced here.
sections.next_action: Run an approved isolated recovery drill and record restore time, data-loss bound, backup lifecycle and alert ownership.

sections.title: PRIVACY BY DESIGN
sections.finding: AI requests are bounded and product events are categorical; a field-by-field purpose/necessity inventory is absent.
sections.next_action: Document collection purposes, recipients, access and retention for every stored field and review additions against it.

sections.title: DATA CLASSIFICATION
sections.finding: The supplied guardrail defines classes, but the app has no complete data-classification inventory mapped to enforcement.
sections.next_action: Classify each table, object bucket, telemetry field and export, then map access/encryption/retention controls.

sections.title: DATA RETENTION
sections.finding: Cleanup exists for temporary connections, but no comprehensive automated lifecycle for drafts, media, logs and retained ledgers is implemented.
sections.next_action: Approve retention periods and implement bounded, observable purge jobs including backup expiry.

sections.title: ACCOUNT DELETION
sections.finding: Assisted erasure requires verified operator input and blocks unresolved billing/publication/storage; no complete self-service workflow exists.
sections.next_action: Build authenticated owner-confirmed deletion with durable provider, billing, storage and secondary-store reconciliation.

sections.title: DATA EXPORT
sections.finding: An allowlisted support export function exists, with no self-service export job or expiring download delivery.
sections.next_action: Add owner-authorized export jobs, tenant-bound expiring access and a media archive with deletion lifecycle.

sections.title: ENCRYPTION
sections.finding: Fernet token encryption exists; database, object and backup encryption plus actual TLS posture require environment evidence.
sections.next_action: Verify managed encryption and TLS settings and plan application-key rotation with tested recovery.

sections.title: SECRET MANAGEMENT
sections.finding: Code uses environment credentials; managed secret storage, environment separation and rotation are not demonstrated.
sections.next_action: Inventory secret consumers and establish rotation/revocation procedures and a secret scanner.

sections.title: MEDIA UPLOAD SECURITY
sections.finding: Upload bytes are bounded and decoded; no systematic metadata stripping or malware policy exists, and public media delivery remains possible. Browser media now uses owner-authenticated previews and short-lived signed downloads. S3 delivery generates presigned URLs instead of returning stored permanent URLs. Existing bucket policy and cache access remain unverified.
sections.next_action: Implement private storage delivery, metadata handling and a documented scan/quarantine policy; verify hostile-media tests.

sections.title: API SECURITY
sections.finding: Authentication, request limits and selected Pydantic schemas exist; some broad dictionaries and unbounded collection patterns remain.
sections.next_action: Inventory routes and enforce strict schemas, response allowlists and budgets, with object-level attack tests.

sections.title: WEBHOOK SECURITY
sections.finding: Stripe signature/replay processing exists. Provider webhook support and asynchronous processing are not comprehensive.
sections.next_action: Document every callback, verify signatures/time/schema, and queue idempotent processing with duplicate-event tests.

sections.title: SSRF
sections.finding: The unused unrestricted fetch_remote helper was removed. Provider-returned URLs and all future ingestion still require an egress review.
sections.next_action: Inventory remaining server egress and constrain provider upload URLs, DNS resolution, redirects, response size and timeouts.

sections.title: FRONTEND SECURITY
sections.finding: CSP, HSTS, framing and origin checks exist; CSP permits inline scripts and styles.
sections.next_action: Move executable inline code to controlled assets/nonces and test CSRF, XSS and browser policy across critical flows.

sections.title: CONTENT PREVIEW
sections.finding: Review snapshots include exact destination, content, attachments and schedule; platform fidelity and accessibility are not independently verified for all formats.
sections.next_action: Exercise every supported format/account/timezone on staging, including unsupported-field warnings and wrong-account prevention.

sections.title: HIGH-RISK ACTION UX
sections.finding: Publish has explicit review, but connection unlink is a direct form submission without a consequence-specific confirmation.
sections.next_action: Add server-enforced confirmation and consequence copy for every high-impact action, with keyboard and screen-reader verification.

sections.title: UNSAVED CHANGES
sections.finding: Studio persistence and revision tests exist; interruption and navigation coverage across all substantive editors is incomplete.
sections.next_action: Test offline save, refresh, navigation, concurrent edits and recovery for each editor; expose clear save state.

sections.title: UX PERFORMANCE
sections.finding: No representative measurements establish the required API latency and Web Vitals targets.
sections.next_action: Measure desktop/mobile p95 reads/writes and LCP/INP/CLS under realistic load, then address bottlenecks.

sections.title: LOADING STATES
sections.finding: Many forms and Studio actions expose loading states; exhaustive asynchronous action coverage has not been verified.
sections.next_action: Inventory asynchronous actions and test busy, repeated click, timeout, success and retry states.

sections.title: ERROR HANDLING
sections.finding: Selected provider exception leaks are now replaced by fixed messages. Error consistency and truthful retry explanations need a full route audit.
sections.next_action: Test all error responses for secrets, outcome clarity, retry policy and recovery action.

sections.title: ACCESSIBILITY
sections.finding: Some semantic and focus behavior exists, but no complete WCAG 2.2 AA audit or automated accessibility CI evidence exists.
sections.next_action: Add automated accessibility checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader/contrast review for critical journeys.

sections.title: RESPONSIVE DESIGN
sections.finding: Prior release notes describe mobile checks; current end-to-end coverage for all critical mobile journeys is incomplete.
sections.next_action: Verify editing, review, publishing, errors and analytics at representative mobile widths and input modes.

sections.title: DESIGN SYSTEM
sections.finding: Shared templates and Studio styles exist; controls remain distributed with duplicated patterns.
sections.next_action: Inventory and consolidate critical shared controls while preserving Zova branding and tested behavior.

sections.title: EMPTY STATES
sections.finding: Connection and Studio empty states exist; a complete feature-by-feature review is outstanding.
sections.next_action: Verify every empty state explains purpose, absence and a usable next action.

sections.title: AI SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
sections.finding: AI proposes drafts/strategy and reviewed publishing uses deterministic validation. Full capability-based policy enforcement depends on missing RBAC.
sections.next_action: Bind every AI action to authenticated workspace capabilities and explicit authority; test bypass attempts.

sections.title: STRUCTURED AI OUTPUT
sections.finding: AI JSON parsing and domain validation exist, but uniform strict provider and execution schemas are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Apply versioned strict schemas and reject extra or invalid action fields before any mutation.

sections.title: AI TENANT ISOLATION
sections.finding: Brand scoping filters normal AI data access; database-enforced isolation and exhaustive adversarial retrieval tests are absent.
sections.next_action: Test cross-tenant IDs/context/attachments/strategy and enforce isolation below application queries.

sections.title: PROMPT INJECTION
sections.finding: Prompts identify media/source text as untrusted, and publishing requires review. Broad adversarial prompt-injection evaluations are absent.
sections.next_action: Test hostile source/media/tool data against deterministic authority controls and ensure secrets cannot enter model context.

sections.title: AI DATA MINIMISATION
sections.finding: AI context has bounds and store=false. Necessity and sensitive-field exclusion need systematic evidence for every model call.
sections.next_action: Capture synthetic outbound payloads and assert minimum approved fields and absence of tokens/billing/other tenants.

sections.title: AI ACTION APPROVAL
sections.finding: Draft/repeat-series review is explicit; capability-specific authority configuration is not complete.
sections.next_action: Validate approval identity, scope, expiry and content binding for every AI-proposed external action.

sections.title: AUDIT LOGGING
sections.finding: Activity rows are mutable, content-bearing and do not constitute a complete immutable actor/action audit trail.
sections.next_action: Add append-only structured audit records for all critical actions with retention, access controls and tamper detection.

sections.title: SECURITY LOGGING
sections.finding: Rate limits exist but there is no comprehensive takeover/anomaly security monitoring and escalation evidence.
sections.next_action: Add minimal security event telemetry and actionable alerts for failed login, denial, privilege and unusual-volume events.

sections.title: OBSERVABILITY
sections.finding: Operational status exposes overdue/unknown jobs and failures; structured logs, distributed traces and paging evidence are incomplete. Operations status now includes content-free counts of overdue and unknown legacy publishing jobs.
sections.next_action: Implement safe structured telemetry, metrics, trace propagation and alert-delivery tests.

sections.title: CORRELATION IDs
sections.finding: Publication support references exist, but there is no universal request-to-job correlation identifier.
sections.next_action: Create and propagate server-generated request/job IDs through responses, durable jobs, audit events and telemetry.

sections.title: RELIABILITY TARGETS
sections.finding: No measured production SLI report establishes the availability and eligible-publishing success targets.
sections.next_action: Define eligible outcomes and provider-outage accounting; instrument and review SLO/error-budget reporting.

sections.title: THIRD-PARTY FAILURE
sections.finding: HTTP timeouts, ambiguous outcome handling and some fallbacks exist; circuit breakers and safe retry/backpressure are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Exercise outages, latency, quota exhaustion and malformed responses per adapter with bounded recovery.

sections.title: PROVIDER ABSTRACTION
sections.finding: Provider dispatch is centralized in social.py; adapters remain coupled in a large module.
sections.next_action: Split adapters behind a stable interface and add provider contract fixtures without changing public behavior.

sections.title: INTERNAL CANONICAL MODEL
sections.finding: Draft/media/review/publication entities exist, alongside separate legacy creator/post routes. Legacy X now uses a versioned durable ledger and explicit submission/status contract; it still needs canonical tenant/identity consolidation.
sections.next_action: Reconcile legacy paths into one canonical publishing contract and versioned payload model.

sections.title: SCALE ARCHITECTURE
sections.finding: A dedicated worker entry point and an embedded-worker disable option now exist. Independent deployment, persistent private media and multi-instance operational assurance remain outstanding.
sections.next_action: Deploy and exercise the independent worker and private object storage after infrastructure approval; prove restart and multi-instance behavior.

sections.title: CONNECTION POOLING
sections.finding: PostgreSQL pool is now explicitly capped at 5 connections by default with no overflow and a finite wait. Fleet-level sizing is not verified.
sections.next_action: Set per-service pool budgets from the actual database capacity and validate saturation/backpressure under load.

sections.title: CACHE DESIGN
sections.finding: Strategy/source state is owner/brand scoped; no complete cache-key and permission-invalidation inventory has been reviewed.
sections.next_action: Inventory all caches and verify tenant prefixes, expiry, invalidation and absence of secret payloads.

sections.title: BILLING SECURITY
sections.finding: Hosted Stripe, verified events and idempotency tests exist; live account configuration and operational reconciliation require current evidence.
sections.next_action: Validate test/live separation, subscription races, duplicate/out-of-order events and current payment setup.

sections.title: ENTITLEMENTS
sections.finding: Explicit allowance functions and usage reservations exist; the complete requested entitlement set and team capability model are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Define canonical entitlements independent of display plans and test concurrent limit enforcement and changes.

sections.title: ADMINISTRATION
sections.finding: Optional customer MFA is implemented but internal operations still use bearer secrets; staff identity, mandatory MFA, separate capabilities and audited support access remain absent.
sections.next_action: Put privileged operations behind verified staff identity, mandatory MFA and least-privilege audited actions; do not force existing customer enrollment.

sections.title: ENVIRONMENT SEPARATION
sections.finding: Render inspection found the TikTok sandbox uses the production database; the existing CS staging service runs a different repository. Tests remain isolated, but an independent deployed Social staging environment is missing.
sections.next_action: Owner paused staging until app approval on 28 September 2026. After the owner confirms approval, revisit STAGING_PLAN.md and obtain cost approval before provisioning; verify distinct data, secrets, storage and credentials before migrations. Continue local work; do not repurpose the shared-database sandbox.

sections.title: CI/CD
sections.finding: CI tests SQLite/PostgreSQL, dependency audit, restore and image build. Lint/type/static security coverage and enforced deployment policy are incomplete. Validation actions are now pinned to verified upstream commits, checkout credentials are not persisted, and jobs/evidence retention are bounded.
sections.next_action: Require Production guardrails plus validation checks in branch protection and hosting; add incremental lint/type/security checks.

sections.title: DEPENDENCY SECURITY
sections.finding: Several dependencies are exact pinned; others are ranges and transitive dependencies are not locked. pip-audit exists in CI. Weekly Dependabot proposals for Python and Actions are configured in the candidate; activation on the default branch remains unverified and no auto-merge is enabled.
sections.next_action: Produce a reproducible complete dependency lock and validate current vulnerability scans with an update/remediation process.

sections.title: SUPPLY CHAIN SECURITY
sections.finding: GitHub ruleset 24140009 is verified Active on main: three GitHub Actions checks required, no bypass actors, up-to-date branches and resolved conversations required, force pushes/deletions blocked. PR approval count is zero; all validation actions are pinned to official upstream commits and checkout credential persistence is disabled. Full dependency/image locks and remaining cloud/registry controls still need assurance.
sections.next_action: Keep the active required checks; establish independent review, finish dependency/image pinning and verify least-privilege cloud/registry access. Optional MFA is authorised; privileged MFA and independent review remain unresolved.

sections.title: TESTING PYRAMID
sections.finding: Substantial synthetic unit/integration suites exist; browser, accessibility and provider contract coverage are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Map critical journeys to each test level and add missing provider/browser security regressions.

sections.title: MANDATORY TENANT ISOLATION TESTS
sections.finding: Cross-owner/brand tests exist and this iteration adds worker and ownership-mutation checks; coverage is not complete across sensitive objects or direct DB access. An additional adversarial worker matrix covers older schedules, including same-owner cross-brand references, wrong-owner/inactive/wrong-platform accounts and malformed media IDs. Provider result reconciliation now binds owner, brand, draft, review and destination before external status access. Legacy job reads/cancellation are creator-scoped. A versioned offline migration now backfills canonical references on all 16 brand-owned tables and installs database write guards for owner/brand/reference immutability. Isolated tests cover direct SQL attacks and existing ORM compatibility; runtime read isolation, RLS, account-level/legacy mapping and deployment remain incomplete. Offline migration lock/statement waits are now bounded and reference previews reject existing incorrect mappings; PostgreSQL contention, cancellation, rollback and retry tests passed at 09c5771; runtime read isolation and deployment remain open. Canonical references now map into all brand-owned ORM records and scoped content reads. Fresh schema setup installs guards; existing populated databases require offline reference migration before startup. Runtime SQLite/PostgreSQL regression and synthetic restore passed at dc55d2b; PostgreSQL RLS and complete service authority remain open.
sections.next_action: Build a complete object/operation attack matrix and run it under restricted PostgreSQL identities with RLS.

sections.title: MANDATORY PUBLISHING TESTS
sections.finding: Reviewed publishing covers duplicates, worker races and uncertainty; legacy routes and all required media/cancellation/provider fault scenarios are incomplete. Older schedules now distinguish definite preflight rejection from uncertain sends; timeout replay tests confirm no automatic retry. Legacy X now has concurrent idempotency/worker, cancellation, changed-authority and timeout/crash tests. The provider-result reconciliation boundary also has adversarial tests.
sections.next_action: Cover every mandatory scenario against all publish entry points with deterministic persisted outcomes.

sections.title: LOAD TESTING
sections.finding: No current 100/1000-user, top-of-hour, ingestion or webhook-spike load evidence is present.
sections.next_action: Run isolated staged load scenarios and verify graceful overload with no duplicate sends or corruption.

sections.title: SECURITY TESTING
sections.finding: Dependency scanning exists; no current external penetration test, full ASVS Level 2 assessment, dynamic/API fuzz or OAuth review evidence exists.
sections.next_action: Scope and complete independent security testing after architectural remediation, recording unresolved findings as blockers.

sections.title: INCIDENT RESPONSE
sections.finding: Operations/rollback notes exist; a complete incident procedure with accountable responders and notification workflow needs approval and exercise.
sections.next_action: Run an incident tabletop covering detection through postmortem, preserving evidence and customer impact analysis.

sections.title: OAUTH COMPROMISE RUNBOOK
sections.finding: No complete OAuth-store compromise runbook, global invalidation, rotation and publishing suspension control is present.
sections.next_action: Implement the emergency control path and exercise provider revocation/key rotation/affected-account identification.

sections.title: DISASTER RECOVERY
sections.finding: Synthetic restore and code rollback guidance exist; all required disaster scenarios and annual exercise evidence are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Document and rehearse database corruption/deletion, region outage, credential compromise and provider failure recovery.

sections.title: GDPR ACCOUNTABILITY
sections.finding: Legal pages and assisted lifecycle functions exist; completeness/current approval of inventory, DPA, subprocessors and DSAR procedures is not verified.
sections.next_action: Obtain accountable privacy review and operational evidence; do not infer legal compliance from code tests.

sections.title: ANALYTICS PRIVACY
sections.finding: Product events and AI usage records favor categorical metadata. Complete third-party analytics/log data-flow exclusion is not verified. Uvicorn access logs now exclude query strings, including signed-media and OAuth parameters; hosting/proxy logging remains unverified.
sections.next_action: Test telemetry allowlists against synthetic credentials, draft text, emails and secret-bearing URLs.

sections.title: SUPPORT DATA ACCESS
sections.finding: Internal status is metadata-only; assisted export/erasure helpers lack enforced per-case staff capability and immutable access records.
sections.next_action: Gate elevated content access with explicit reason, verified support role and immutable audit.

sections.title: PRODUCT TRUST
sections.finding: Review shows account identity and publication results; scopes, last access, actor attribution and automation visibility are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Expose accurate connection permissions/access and action provenance with clear automation status.

sections.title: AUTOMATION GUARDRAILS
sections.finding: Finite recurring plans declare timing/mode and reviewed snapshots; uniform trigger/condition/limits/authority declarations are incomplete.
sections.next_action: Define and display a versioned automation policy enforced by workers and approvals.

sections.title: AUTOMATION KILL SWITCH
sections.finding: Series can pause/cancel, but workspace-wide automated publishing pause and system-wide emergency switch are absent.
sections.next_action: Add durable owner and operations switches enforced immediately before new dispatch, with audited changes and in-flight caveats.

sections.title: SAFE DEFAULTS
sections.finding: Marketing consent is off and publishing requires review. Public media configuration and MFA defaults do not meet the complete safe-default requirement. Owner authorised optional MFA on 9 October 2026. Existing accounts remain unchanged until enrollment; privileged MFA defaults are unresolved. Browser media now uses owner-authenticated previews and short-lived signed downloads. S3 delivery generates presigned URLs instead of returning stored permanent URLs. Existing bucket policy and cache access remain unverified.
sections.next_action: Verify private storage policies, explicit opt-in automation and privileged MFA defaults without forcing customer enrollment.

sections.title: USER CONTROL
sections.finding: Users manage connections/profile/billing and series. Team roles, direct deletion and direct exports are missing or assisted-only.
sections.next_action: Implement accessible authenticated self-service lifecycle/team/automation controls with recovery and audit.

sections.title: RELEASE SEVERITY MODEL
sections.finding: This assessment applies P0â€“P3 and blocks all unresolved applicable sections; previously deployed code has not been certified against the model.
sections.next_action: Assign accountable owners and verify release policy is required in repository and hosting controls.

sections.title: PRODUCTION RELEASE GATE
sections.finding: The fail-closed production check is running and required on main by verified GitHub ruleset 24140009. Application/PostgreSQL/restore/image checks passed for the first candidate. Hosting enforcement and all domain closure evidence remain outstanding.
sections.next_action: Verify the actual production hosting gate, preserve mandatory repository checks and close every applicable domain requirement. Keep remediation on the unmerged draft PR.

sections.title: ZOVA'S TEN NON-NEGOTIABLES
sections.finding: The ten non-negotiables cannot be certified while tenant, legacy publishing, queue, audit and recovery requirements remain unresolved.
sections.next_action: Close underlying blockers with independently reviewable evidence; do not waive them based on a successful build.

sections.title: TARGET PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE
sections.finding: API, ORM and provider layers exist; restricted PostgreSQL/RLS, independent worker/queue, private object storage and central telemetry remain incomplete.
sections.next_action: Migrate incrementally to the target architecture with compatibility, recovery and failure tests at each stage.

sections.title: ENGINEERING DEFINITION OF DONE
sections.finding: The definition of done is now versioned and checked through the register; complete operational and product acceptance evidence is absent.
sections.next_action: Require evidence-backed closure, repeat the full release gate on the exact candidate and archive approved release evidence.
